title: Vercel and Shopify make agents first-class shoppers
description: Agents already shop on the web, but they often use pages and tools originally built for people and search engines. Building a better shopping experience for agents means treating them as first-class shoppers, with product information they can read directly and tools designed for agents to shop. Today, Vercel Shop , our open source Next.js storefront template for Shopify , is generally available. Teams can launch storefronts optimized for how people, search engines, and agents interact with them. Vercel Shop is built on Shopify’s Hydrogen SDK . The SDK gives teams access to the store’s product catalog, cart and order management, payments, and checkout to build custom storefronts. Earlier this year, Vercel and Shopify announced plans to rebuild Hydrogen to work across JavaScript frameworks. Today, the rebuilt SDK is generally available. Give agents the information and tools they need Vercel Shop makes product pages available as machine-readable content , including price, availability, and options. The same product URL can serve a visual page to people or product information that agents can read without interpreting the page’s layout. The template also includes structured data embedded in pages and sitemaps to help search and answer engines discover and understand the products. Shopify co-developed the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), which gives agents a standard way to search a store’s catalog, read product details, check availability, build a cart, and get a checkout link. Vercel Shop makes these capabilities discoverable at the merchant’s own domain, so agents can use MCP to search products and build carts without navigating the site. Customize the experience for all customers Vercel Shop brings the store’s product catalog, cart, and checkout together with a Next.js storefront, product information and shopping tools for agents, and a shopping assistant powered by eve . The storefront and assistant live in the same codebase, so teams can customize the store’s design and how the assistant helps shoppers. Skills included in the template guide coding agents through setup, customization, and template updates. Teams can create an experience where shoppers browse product pages or ask the assistant to find products and add them to their cart. Both share the same cart, so shoppers keep what they’ve added as they move between experiences. Storefronts built with Shopify and Vercel Today, we launched our merch store at vercel.store with limited-edition drops. It’s built on Vercel Shop. The store’s shopping agent helps shoppers find products, add them to their cart, and continue to checkout. Shopify, Next.js, and Vercel already power storefronts for brands including AG1, Bombas, and PAIGE. When PAIGE re-architected its ecommerce platform , it saw a 22% increase in revenue and a 76% increase in conversion over Black Friday and Cyber Monday, with no downtime. Get started with Vercel Shop Create a storefront: Get started with Vercel Shop . Check the documentation to connect your Shopify store and configure the storefront. Read more

title: Perplexity's Decider V1.2 models now available on AI Gateway
description: Perplexity Decider V1.2 27B and Decider Flash V1.2 4B are now available on AI Gateway . Both are multimodal decision models for classifying content, routing requests, and scoring text, structured records, and images. The models answer typed questions with probabilities. Boolean questions return the likelihood of yes, Choice questions select from categories you define, and Score questions assess content against an ordered rubric. Your application can use those results to route a support ticket, flag a damaged product, or send an uncertain decision for human review. Multiple questions can share the same input in one request. Decider V1.2 27B ( perplexity/pplx-decider-v1.2 ) is the larger model, for nuanced judgments and detailed rubrics. Decider Flash V1.2 4B ( perplexity/pplx-decider-flash-v1.2 ) is the smaller model, for high-volume labeling, filtering, and routing with clear criteria. The examples below use perplexity/pplx-decider-v1.2 and check the same delivery report through the AI SDK , the Decisions API , and the TypeSafe-compatible API : For image input, embed base64 image_url objects in JSON state through the AI SDK or TypeSafe-compatible API. See Perplexity's image format and the decision models documentation for request formats and question types. Explore Decider V1.2 27B in the model playground , or try Decider Flash V1.2 4B . Use AI Gateway to call models with one API key and monitor usage and cost in one place. Decision requests are recorded in request logs and included in spend budgets . Inference uses provider pricing without a markup or platform fee. This also applies when you supply your own provider credentials through BYOK . Browse the decision model catalog to see the available options. Read more

title: Reflection AI's Beam now available on AI Gateway for free
description: Beam from Reflection AI , previously available in stealth as stealth/cat-jam , is now available on AI Gateway . Beam is free to use for a limited time during the launch period when serviced by Reflection AI. Beam is an low latency US open-weight reasoning model for coding and agentic tasks, with weights released under Apache 2.0 . Beam supports tool calling and structured outputs , with a 1M-token context window for code, documents, and conversation history. Reasoning effort is adjustable. Beam is designed for speed, activating only 23B of its 501B parameters per token and avoiding tokens a task doesn't need, so it tends to reach answers sooner than larger open models. There are 2 ways to access Beam for free: Using the standard model name ( reflection/beam with provider reflection ). When the free period ends, the model slug will automatically transfer over to pricing with no downtime. Using the -free suffix to the standard name ( reflection/beam-free ). The model will stop serving when the free offer ends. To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Then select reflection/beam or reflection/beam-free in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details. Try Beam in the model playground . AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , Zero Data Retention support , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. Read more

title: Python on Vercel is now generally available
description: Python on Vercel is now generally available. Build and run Python applications with the frameworks, libraries, and tools you already use. Vercel automatically detects supported frameworks and configures the build and deployment. Your applications run on Fluid compute, which manages concurrent requests and scales with traffic. Idiomatic Python SDKs let you work with storage, queues, durable workflows, and AI models directly from Python. For full-stack projects, the Python backend and frontend share a workflow for local development, preview deployments, and production releases. Our goals for Python on Vercel Ten months ago, we set out to make Vercel the best place to build and run Python applications . We wanted the experience to fit how Python developers already work, with three goals guiding our decisions: Idiomatic Python SDKs. Working with Vercel infrastructure should feel familiar to Python developers, with APIs that use type annotations, async / await , and context managers. A shared workflow for both the frontend and backend. Python applications often include a JavaScript frontend, so developers should be able to run both locally, review them in the same preview deployment, and release or roll them back together. Compatibility with the Python ecosystem. The runtime should use CPython, the standard Python interpreter, on Linux to preserve compatibility with the packages and tools Python developers already rely on. The first test of those goals is what happens when you deploy a Python application on Vercel: its framework, dependencies, and project structure should guide how it’s built and run. Deploying Python applications on Vercel We’ve worked to make Python feel native on Vercel. Vercel reads your project’s dependency files, including those managed by uv , and automatically detects frameworks such as FastAPI, Flask, Django, and FastHTML. Framework defined infrastructure configures builds and request routing, with framework-specific support for serving static assets through the CDN. For applications with a frontend, Vercel Services brings both parts into one project. Running vercel dev starts them together, and shared previews let you test backend changes with the frontend that uses them. For long-running workers that pull jobs from queues or databases, Vercel Daemons keeps your containers running with your Python code along with any of its packages, and system dependencies. Python SDKs for Vercel infrastructure A Python backend might need to store files, send messages, run durable workflows, or call AI models. We’ve built Python SDKs for these tasks, with APIs that follow the conventions of the language: These SDKs work alongside your framework and libraries, and the example below shows how they connect within a full-stack application. Start building with Python on Vercel Whether you’re starting a new project or deploying existing code, the framework guides cover setup and deployment on Vercel. For a guided full-stack project, the Python on Vercel course walks through building a FastAPI backend and Next.js frontend, then deploying them together with Services. To show how these pieces work together, I built a collaborative web application to create and browse Python notebooks. It lets people create their own notebooks, publish them for others to browse or fork, and work with an AI assistant to write and run Python code. The application pairs a Vite frontend with a FastAPI backend and uses PostgreSQL for notebook source and chat history. Services keeps the frontend and backend in one deployment, with the frontend served through the CDN. Here’s how the main parts connect: Editing and running code: When a signed-in user opens their notebook in the editor, FastAPI creates or reuses a Vercel Sandbox running Jupyter, keeping user code isolated from the application backend. The browser connects directly to Jupyter, while mounted Drives provide the Python dependencies and workspace files. Saving and publishing: The browser periodically sends the current notebook to FastAPI. FastAPI saves the source in PostgreSQL, renders changes as HTML, and uploads the result to Blob, so people can read published notebooks through the CDN without starting a Python kernel. Sharing updates: After publishing a change, FastAPI sends a message through Vercel Queues. Each backend instance with connected browsers receives the notification and sends updated notebook listings over WebSockets, so people see changes without reloading. Assisting with code: The agent uses AI SDK for Python and runs inside Vercel Workflows, which saves execution state and retries failed steps. Chat history stays in PostgreSQL, while notebook editing and execution tools work through the connected browser, which sends results back through FastAPI to resume the workflow. The source code on GitHub includes the complete application and its deployment configuration. You can use it to explore these integrations or as a starting point for your own Python application. Investing in the Python community Last December, the Gel Data team, led by me and Elvis Pranskevichus, joined Vercel to build Python support and continue our open-source work. At the same time, we announced our sponsorship of the Python Software Foundation and committed to funding one year of Serhiy Storchaka’s CPython maintenance through the foundation. Serhiy has authored over 600 commits to CPython’s main branch so far in 2026. We also sponsored PyCon US and EuroPython this year, where the team and I met Python developers and heard where they were getting stuck. Those conversations help us figure out what to fix next. We also published PEP 827 , which, if accepted, would add type manipulation features that could help frameworks such as FastAPI offer simpler APIs with less boilerplate and more precise type checking. What’s next for Python on Vercel We’re continuing to improve Python SDKs, runtime performance, and development workflows for both people and coding agents. If you run into a deployment issue or find something missing in the Python SDKs, share your feedback in Vercel Community so the team can use it to guide that work.
